title: The Liver
hook: The liver is the body's chemical plant — it filters toxins, makes bile, stores fuel, and runs hundreds of jobs no other organ can.
key_points: The liver is the largest internal organ and performs over 500 distinct functions.
It detoxifies the blood, breaking down drugs, alcohol, and metabolic waste.
It produces bile, which the gut needs to digest and absorb fats.
It stores energy as glycogen and releases glucose to keep blood sugar steady.
It can regenerate, regrowing to full size from a fraction of its tissue.
content_html: The liver is the body's chemical plant — the largest internal organ and one of the busiest, running an estimated 500-plus jobs. Blood from the gut flows through it first, so it can strip out toxins, break down drugs and alcohol, and process the nutrients you just absorbed before they reach the rest of the body.
extra_html: As Encyclopaedia Britannica describes, the liver wears many hats at once. It manufactures bile, which the small intestine needs to digest fats. It acts as a fuel bank, storing surplus sugar as glycogen and releasing glucose when blood sugar dips, helping the body hold a steady internal balance. It builds blood proteins, stores certain vitamins and iron, and neutralizes ammonia and other waste so the kidneys can flush it out. Remarkably, the liver can also regenerate, regrowing to full size from a fraction of its tissue — a property that makes living-donor liver transplants possible.

related.title: The Digestive System
related.hook: From the first bite to the final absorption, your digestive tract is a one-way assembly line that turns food into fuel your cells can use.

related.title: What Blood Does
related.hook: Blood looks like a single red liquid, but it's really a fleet of specialized parts — each cell type and the fluid itself carrying out a different life-sustaining job.

related.title: Homeostasis: Staying Balanced
related.hook: Your body works hard to keep its inside world steady — temperature, water, blood sugar — no matter what's happening outside. That balancing act is homeostasis.

flashcards.prompt: Why is the liver called the body's chemical plant?
flashcards.back_html: Because it runs hundreds of chemical jobs — detoxifying the blood, making bile, storing energy, and building proteins — all in one organ.

flashcards.prompt: What does the liver produce to help digest fats?
flashcards.explanation_html: The liver makes bile, which is stored in the gallbladder and released into the gut to break large fat droplets into smaller ones the body can absorb.

flashcards.prompt: What unusual ability sets the liver apart from most organs?

choices.text: It can regenerate, regrowing from a fraction of itself
It can beat on its own without nerves
It works without any blood supply

flashcards.explanation_html: The liver is remarkably regenerative — even after losing much of its mass, the remaining tissue can grow back to a functional size.
